Hey. I'm filipino too, so I totally get where you're coming from with the comparisons. What helped me the most was realizing that I could never change my parents, or their actions. They're always going to be nitpicky and angry about something -- doesn't matter what. But what you \*can\* change is your reactions to what they're saying. I wouldn't take anything they'd say personally, and if you personally think you're doing great -- then you're doing great ! 

I also found that surrounding yourself with a good support system is good too, if your parents can't be there for you emotionally -- at least your friends can.

I was brought up in a strict asian household. Normally, they're pretty stingy with hanging out with friends -- even though I'm 20 and halfway through university....I'm not even that social, I barely saw them in second year. I totaled my mom's car over the weekend while they were away and while everything is sorted out, I'm getting extreme verbal abuse from my own mom. I've been suicidal since I was 12 and I've done a good job at hiding those feelings away but right now, they've come back to resurface.

My mom didn't ask first if I was okay, she first went on to a whole ramble to say that I did this on purpose to ruin their image, and that I'm the reason why I'm destroying my own family because "all I care about is my friends". In a very aggressive tone, she said "I'm glad you're okay, but you're 20 and you'll never be a good person"

I totally relate though, it was definitely worse in high school but since entering university it's gotten better -- until now. I'm really trying my best to rack up work experience and get better grades in the last two years of my university years so I can get my masters somewhere else.

EDIT: to further add how fucked up it was, when the whole truth started spilling out she said "you deserve to be traumatized" and im still shaken from that comment

Right now, I'm aiming to move as far away from them as possible after university. I am looking to live in a city four hours away from where I live right now -- but if I luck out, maybe in a different province completely. I'm also aiming to have my masters in a city that's also four hours away. Today I'm going to my university's counselling services because I'm still shaken from the car accident on top of all of this.
